backtest_protocol: docs/backtesting.md canonical three fixed windows. Core uses canonical snapshots; Space variants use exp-20260510-028 augmented Space snapshots. The accepted_before variant reproduces exp-20260513-015 policy semantics.

before_variant.target_definition: government_space_contract event profile and peer momentum leader

decision_rationale: The satellite-connectivity theme scalar did not clear the three-window gate on top of exp-20260513-015. Keep Space theme-segment risk allocation limited to the accepted launch/lunar helper.

gate1.known_bias: Space candidate snapshots are frozen historical replay copies built from a 2026-05-10 research universe. Theme fields are production-visible registry metadata, but any accepted Space change must remain default-off until forward evidence matures.

accepted_multi_event_depth.target_definition: official Space ticker with at least two official, non-attention event seed rows

government_contract_profile.target_definition: official Space ticker with government_space_contract from an official non-attention source

peer_momentum_state.source: accepted Space basket momentum enrichment from exp-20260511-115 stack

gate_questions.1_alpha_hypothesis: risk allocation: scale official Space signals whose registry theme_segment is satellite_connectivity.

2_history_check.exp-20260512-032: Accepted launch_lunar theme top-up; this tests a different theme_segment and does not retune launch_lunar.
2_history_check.exp-20260513-014/015: Accepted customer-source/government-contract peer-leader helpers are fixed as the before stack.
2_history_check.exp-20260513-019: Rejected customer-source peer-nonleader complement; this run uses theme segment rather than source/peer complement.
2_history_check.llm_soft_ranking: Still label-limited, so this run avoids LLM scoring.

gate_questions.3_single_causal_variable: space_satellite_connectivity_theme_risk_scalar. Candidate pool, accepted Space stack, source/peer helpers, targets, stops, ranking, LLM/news, and live slots stay fixed.
gate_questions.4_acceptance_standard: docs/backtesting.md three fixed windows; require positive aggregate EV/PnL versus exp-015 accepted stack, at least 2/3 improved EV windows, no EV-regressed window, max drawdown drift <= 0.5 pp, survival >= 5%, >=50 total trades, nonzero adjusted signals, and non-1.0 scalar.

hypothesis: The accepted Space stack has shown value in production-visible catalyst quality fields. Satellite-connectivity signals may deserve a separate risk allocation because their regulatory/direct-to-device catalysts differ from launch/lunar and data/defense catalysts, without adding tickers, changing ranking, or using LLM soft-ranking.
interpretation: The satellite-connectivity theme scalar did not clear the three-window gate on top of exp-20260513-015. Keep Space theme-segment risk allocation limited to the accepted launch/lunar helper.

llm_metrics.why_not_llm_soft_ranking: Space soft-ranking remains label-limited; this run uses deterministic production-visible theme metadata.

next_evidence_needed: If rejected, do not add a satellite-connectivity theme top-up on these frozen snapshots. Future Space alpha should use forward replacement value by catalyst family/source/peer/theme bucket or a new production-visible official catalyst-quality field.
